{{short description|Notation used to describe knots based on operations on tangles}}

[[File:Conway tangle transformations and operations.svg|thumb|300px|The full set of fundamental transformations and operations on 2-tangles, alongside the elementary tangles 0, ∞, ±1 and ±2.]]
[[File:Blue Trefoil Knot.png|thumb|The [[trefoil knot]] has Conway notation [3].]]
In [[knot theory]], '''Conway notation''', invented by [[John Horton Conway]], is a way of describing [[Knot (mathematics)|knot]]s that makes many of their properties clear. It composes a knot using certain operations on [[tangle (mathematics)|tangle]]s to construct it.

==Basic concepts==
===Tangles===

In Conway notation, the [[tangle (mathematics)|tangle]]s are generally algebraic 2-tangles.  This means their tangle diagrams consist of 2 arcs and 4 points on the edge of the diagram; furthermore, they are built up from [[rational tangle]]s using the Conway operations.

[The following seems to be attempting to describe only integer or 1/n rational tangles]
Tangles consisting only of positive crossings are denoted by the number of crossings, or if there are only negative crossings it is denoted by a negative number. If the arcs are not crossed, or can be transformed into an uncrossed position with the [[Reidemeister move]]s, it is called the 0 or ∞ tangle, depending on the orientation of the tangle.

===Operations on tangles===

If a tangle, ''a'', is reflected on the NW-SE line, it is denoted by ''<sup>−</sup>a''. (Note that this is different from a tangle with a negative number of crossings.) Tangles have three [[binary operation]]s, ''sum'', ''product'', and ''ramification'',<ref>"[http://www.mi.sanu.ac.rs/vismath/sl/l14.htm Conway notation]", ''mi.sanu.ac.rs''.</ref> however all can be explained using tangle addition and negation. The tangle product, ''a b'', is equivalent to ''<sup>−</sup>a+b''. and ramification or ''a,b'', is equivalent to ''<sup>−</sup>a+<sup>−</sup>b''.

==Advanced concepts==
Rational [[tangle (mathematics)|tangles]] are equivalent [[if and only if]] their fractions are equal. An accessible proof of this fact is given in (Kauffman and Lambropoulou 2004). A number before an asterisk, ''*'', denotes the polyhedron number; multiple asterisks indicate that multiple polyhedra of that number exist.<ref>{{Knot Atlas|Conway Notation}}</ref>
